resources.string: Shown while this phone is hosting or listening in a group
%1$s couldn\'t load the song and will skip it
%1$s is running a different SongSync version. Update both phones.
Turn on Location in your phone\'s settings to find nearby phones
SongSync is missing the Nearby devices permission (Nearby code %1$d). Allow it in Settings → Permissions and try again.
Finding groups needs precise location (Nearby code %1$d). In Settings → Permissions → Location, choose “Allow only while using the app” and turn on “Use precise location”.
Bluetooth or Wi-Fi is off or busy. Turn them on and try again.
Another app is using Nearby right now. Close it and try again.
Keep SongSync open while connecting so it can keep playing with the screen off.
Play the same song on every phone, perfectly in sync.
Pick the music. Other phones join you.
Listen along with a nearby host.

SongSync connects phones directly over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, which needs the Nearby devices permission. Google\'s Nearby service also requires location to find other phones: choose “Precise” when asked. SongSync never reads or stores your location.
SongSync connects phones directly over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. On this Android version that needs the precise Location permission. SongSync never reads or stores your location.
Some permissions are off for SongSync. In the app settings, allow Nearby devices, and for Location allow it while using the app with “Use precise location” on.
On this Android version, phones can only find each other while Location is switched on.
Ask the host to tap “Host a group”. Keep Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on.

Check that the host tapped “Host a group” and is close by. Still nothing? On this phone, turn Bluetooth off and back on, then tap Search again: some phones stop hearing nearby devices after scanning for a long time.
The search pauses after a few minutes so it doesn\'t drain the battery or tire out Bluetooth. Ask the host to tap “Host a group”, then search again.
Search for a song to start the party
Search failed. Check your internet connection.
The music stops on every phone.
Waiting for %1$s to pick a song…
Paused on this phone. The group keeps playing.
If this phone sounds early or late, nudge it until the echo disappears. Saved for %1$s.

Each phone chirps in turn while this phone listens, twice, and a phone is corrected only when both measurements agree. Put all phones close to this one (within about 30 cm) or all at the same distance from it: sound takes 3 ms per metre, which would be measured too.
Big differences between phones can also come from distance (3 ms per metre). If the phones were not all close to this one, or at the same distance, calibrate again that way.
Listening… each phone chirps in turn. Keep the phones close to this one (or all at the same distance) and the room quiet.
%1$s: not heard. Turn its volume up and try again.
%1$s: measured %2$+d ms, too large to be real for its speaker, so not applied. Check its volume and try again.
%1$s: skipped, it is paused on that phone. Tap “Rejoin the music” there and try again.
Saved for each phone\'s current speaker or headphones. Run it again after switching to a Bluetooth speaker.
This phone\'s microphone is not available.
The calibration sound didn\'t start in time. Try again.
Couldn\'t hear the chirps. Turn up the volume on every phone and try again.
Auto-calibration needs the microphone to hear the phones. Nothing is recorded or sent.
The host couldn\'t hear this phone during calibration. Turn up its volume and try again.
%1$s: two measurements disagreed (%2$+d ms, then %3$+d ms), so nothing was changed. Keep the room quiet and the phones still, then try again.
A phone joined, left or paused during calibration. Try again.
Echo calibration reset on every phone. They now play uncorrected.
The host reset echo calibration. This phone now plays uncorrected.
Excellent: the phones sound like one speaker. Nothing was changed.
Good: tight enough for music. Nothing was changed.
Acceptable, but an echo may be audible on sharp sounds. Nothing was changed; try Auto-calibrate echo.
Audible echo. Nothing was changed; try Auto-calibrate echo, then check again.
Set automatically by “Auto-calibrate echo” on the host. Fine-tune only if this phone still sounds early or late.
No other phones yet. They can join from “Join a group”.
New phones can\'t join. Phones already in the group can still reconnect.
Different file than this phone (may be offset)
Playing through Bluetooth adds 100–300 ms that only Auto-calibrate echo (on the host) can measure. Calibrate again after connecting or switching speakers.
Chosen by the host; every phone streams the same file.
Forget what SongSync learned about this phone\'s speaker and headphones.
Show clock offset, link round-trip time and sync error in the player.
